text:
Corridor #3 - begins at its westerly end from an interchange located at approximately midway between Ramsey Avenue and Grange Avenue.
This freeway access interchange to the Interstate System at I-94 would be located 3/4 miles north of the College Avenue interchange and 1-1/4 miles south of the directional interchange at Layton Avenue. At the present time an interchange constructed in this vicinity would be virtually free of development. The area west of I-94, to accommodate a portion of the interchange, is undeveloped lands with an open 100 foot wide Oak Creek storm water drainage channel running diagonally across it.
East of I-94 a freeway facility could fit into an existing 550 foot slot of undeveloped land between Parnell Avenue and adjacent subdivision. It would, however, abut the City of Milwaukee's Hamlin Garland Elementary School property located to the south. The most feasible alignment in this corridor would be approximately 250 feet from the school building. North-east of the school at 14th Street a greenhouse and attendant buildings have already been displaced. The remaining lands between I-94 and 13th Street are still undeveloped.
The subdivision north of Parnell Avenue is primarily single family residential with some two, four, and eight family units located along 13th Street. Between 13th Street and the C.M. St. P. & P. Railroad is vacant land presently in use as a dump site, truck storage yard, and railroad siding area. The area is zoned for light industrial use.
Adjacent, but west of the railroad tracks, is the Wisconsin Electric Power Company's high voltage transmission tower lines. These lines would have to be adjusted since the freeway facility would be elevated at 13th Street, the railroad tracks, and 6th Street.
